## Read the raw data

Read from `../data/raw/`.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Load MusicBrainz recording data for five test songs
musicbrainz <- read_csv(
  "../data/raw/musicbrainz_multiple_songs.csv"
)

# Examine the data
glimpse(musicbrainz)

# Count the number of candidate recordings for each song
musicbrainz |>
  count(searched_title, searched_artist)
```

## Clean each source

Types, formats, missing values, duplicates.

### MusicBrainz

```{r}
# Count missing release years
sum(is.na(musicbrainz$release_year))

# Check for duplicate recording IDs
sum(duplicated(musicbrainz$recording_id))

# Summarize release years
summary(musicbrainz$release_year)
```

```{r}
# Clean recording information
musicbrainz_clean <- musicbrainz |>
  mutate(
    searched_title = trimws(searched_title),
    searched_artist = trimws(searched_artist),
    title = trimws(title),
    release_year = as.integer(release_year)
  ) |>
  distinct(searched_title, searched_artist,
           recording_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Examine cleaned data
glimpse(musicbrainz_clean)

# Check number of rows after cleaning
nrow(musicbrainz_clean)
```

MusicBrainz may return multiple recording entries for the same song.
These entries are retained when they have different recording IDs.
Missing release years are preserved rather than replaced with
unverified values.

The release years in this dataset represent dates associated with
candidate recordings, not necessarily the original release years
of the songs.

## Save the cleaned data

Write to `../data/processed/`.

```{r}
# Create processed data folder if needed
dir.create(
  "../data/processed",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# Save cleaned MusicBrainz data for later steps
write_csv(
  musicbrainz_clean,
  "../data/processed/musicbrainz_recordings_clean.csv"
)
```
